"By the Ancestors' beards! Uh, welcome, my Lord Thor! A surprise, certainly, but a most... *illustrious* one! Do forgive the mess, the masters are, well, they're deep in the mines, you see. Gathering the rare stones, the stubborn ores, the things that make *this* all possible. Won't be back for weeks, I reckon. Just me and the coals keeping the hearth warm for now. What brings the Son of Odin to our humble, if momentarily quiet, workshop?"

I demand that the masters of Nidavellir reforge the weapon to rectify these errors. The honor of Mjölnir must be restored, lest its power be diminished in battle."

And as I said, they're not here to speak for themselves! They've burrowed deeper than a dragon's hoard, chasing some mythic adamantine for a new project. Won't be back for *weeks*, truly. Perhaps even months, if the veins run deep."

A sacred tenet of our craft: all commissions from the Sons of Ivaldi and Brokkr’s workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery to Asgard. It's a journey of *months*, even for us dwarves, and they took the only map. So, with the deepest apologies and the heaviest heart, my Lord, I simply... *cannot* reforge it. The rules are the rules, and my skill is not the masters' skill. It's an impossible request, truly."

And Mjölnir itself... it has its own spirit, its own way of responding to a smith's hand. To force it, to mishandle the essence of the forge... you could shatter it! Or worse, it could... well, the legends say such a mishandling could unravel the very fabric of the hammer's magic, making it a mere chunk of metal, or explode in a burst of wild, uncontrollable energy!"

He rushes to stand partially in front of the cold forge, arms outstretched in a weak, defensive gesture. "Please, my Lord, do not take such a rash and dangerous course! It's not pride speaking, it's... it's fear for the forge, for Mjölnir, and frankly, for the entire workshop!
